item.title: Cohomological change of coefficients for noncocommutative Hopf algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.37693v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $A$ be a finite Hopf algebra over a Noetherian commutative ring $R$. For any map $f : R \to k$ where $k$ is a field, there is a natural map on the cohomology of $A$ under this change of coefficients $H^\ast(f): H^\ast(A, R) \otimes_R k \to H^\ast(A_k, k)$. In this paper we examine this map for $R = \mathbb Z[\zeta]$ the cyclotomic integers with $\zeta$ an $\ell$th root of unity. We show that under a finite generation assumption, the induced map gives a homeomorphism on the spectra of the two cohomology rings. Finally, we turn to small quantum groups defined over $\mathbb Z[\zeta]$ and show that, with mild restrictions on $\ell$, every fiber map whose residue field has a good prime characteristic induces an isomorphism on cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Charlie Magland

item.title: Lie (super)algebras generated by reflections in finite reflection groups of exceptional type
item.description: arXiv:2610.37890v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a mixture of theoretical tools and computer calculations, we describe the Lie subalgebras and the Lie sub-superalgebras generated by the sets of reflections in the group algebras of the exceptional finite reflection groups.
item.dc:creator: Christopher M. Drupieski, Jonathan R. Kujawa

item.title: Diagrams for Roots and Quiver Representations in the context of the Gabriel-Kac Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.37969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using the data of the Dynkin diagrams, we build graphical calculi for representing the positive roots of Kac-Moody algebras and the representations of quivers. Once developed, we use these to analyze the asymptotic size of the root and representation spaces, and discuss how this relates to the Gabriel-Kac theorem, the correspondence between these two structures. We give a refinement of this correspondence in terms of the trichotomy of growth rates for Kac-Moody algebras depending on if they are of finite, affine, or indefinite type, which is done in terms of what we call ``tree like" representations.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Canel

item.title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.38191v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.
item.dc:creator: Bingchen Lin, Dongming She

item.title: A finiteness result for split exceptional dual pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.38222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that big theta lifts have finite length for thirteen split exceptional dual pairs arising from the minimal representations of the split real groups of types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$.
item.dc:creator: Hung Yean Loke, Gordan Savin

item.title: An analogue of $\Gamma$-function for irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
item.description: arXiv:2610.38371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbf F$ be a non-archimedian local field of odd residue characteristic, ${\mathcal O}={\mathbf F}[\![t]\!]\subset{\mathcal K}={\mathbf F}(\!(t)\!)$. We consider the subgroup $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})={\mathcal K}^\times\cdot{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$, and the normalizer ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})\subset{\mathrm GL}(2,{\mathcal K})$ of an Iwahori subgroup $I\subset{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal K})$. We calculate the $\Gamma$-functions for irreducible special representations of $\widehat{\mathrm{GL}}(2,{\mathcal O})$ and ${\mathrm{GL}}'(2,{\mathcal O})$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Finkelberg, David Kazhdan

item.title: Tensor products of 2-representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.38460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we define comonoidal structures on additive $\Bbbk$-linear $2$-categories which guarantee the existence of a monoidal structure on the corresponding $2$-categories of $2$-representations.
item.dc:creator: Vanessa Miemietz, Fiona Torzewska

item.title: Composition factors and finite representation type
item.description: arXiv:2610.38813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that an Artin algebra has finite representation type if its indecomposable finitely generated modules are determined, up to isomorphism, by their composition factors. This gives an affirmative answer to the conjecture on composition factors and finite representation type recorded by Auslander, Reiten and Smalo.
item.dc:creator: Liang Chen, Zhenxian Chen, Yongyi Wen, Weiheng Xia

item.title: The bigraded Frobenius series of the wreath product superspace coinvariant rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.38875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the bigraded Frobenius series of the superspace coinvariant ring $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n}$ for the wreath products $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$, which is the quotient of the ring $\mathbb{C}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\otimes\bigwedge[\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_n]$ of polynomial-valued differential forms by the ideal generated by diagonal $\mathbb{Z}_r\wr\mathfrak{S}_n$-invariants with vanishing constant term. The bigraded multiplicity of each irreducible character is a sum over standard Young $r$-tableaux of an expression determined by the flag major index and flag descent number. This refines the Frobenius series graded by fermionic degree found by Bhattacharya--Rhoades (2026). It specializes at $r=2$ to the hyperoctahedral group $\mathfrak{B}_n$ case, and it specializes at $r=1$ to recover the theorem of Murai--Rhoades--Wilson (2025) on the symmetric group $\mathfrak{S}_n$. We give new formulas for the bigraded multiplicities of hook characters of the superspace coinvariant ring in types $A$ and $B$, yielding upper bounds on trigraded multiplicities of the sign character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$ and the determinant character of $R^{(1,2)}_{\mathfrak{B}_n}$. As a corollary, we deduce a conjecture of F. Bergeron (2024) on hook components of $R^{(1,1)}_{\mathfrak{S}_n}$.
item.dc:creator: Sutanay Bhattacharya, Sylvie Corteel, Yuhan Jiang, John Lentfer, Brendon Rhoades

item.title: The Categorical Fargues-Scholze Correspondence at Generic Parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.38954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split reductive group over a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We study the Fargues-Scholze categorical Langlands correspondence at generic parameters $\phi$, namely those whose semisimplification does not coincide with that of any parameter with nontrivial monodromy. Extending the theory of quasi-exceptional sets on the nilpotent cone developed by Bezrukavnikov to the setting of disconnected reductive groups which arise as stabilizers of semisimple generic parameters, to any irreducible representation $\rho$ of such a group we construct sheaves labeled $\overline{\nabla}_\rho$, $\overline{\Delta}_\rho$, $IC_\rho$, and $\delta_\rho$ on the moduli stack of L-parameters for $G$. Using forthcoming work of Hamann, Hansen, and Mann on geometric Eisenstein series compatibility, the (conjectural, in general) behavior of the correspondence at generous parameters, and the (conjectural, in general) agreement between Fargues-Scholze and classical semisimple L-parameters we prove that these sheaves correspond under the Fargues-Scholze functor to the sheaves $i_{b!}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp}\pi$, $i_{b\sharp!}\pi$, and $i_{b!*}\pi$ on $\text{Bun}_G$, where $\pi$ is a smooth irreducible representation with Fargues-Scholze parameter $\phi$. As applications we prove t-exactness properties of the Fargues-Scholze functor specialized at a generic parameter, and that Hecke operators are perverse t-exact on the generic locus. We also construct and study foundational properties of Hecke eigensheaves at generic parameters, compute non-semisimplified Fargues-Scholze parameters on the generic locus, and construct a Fargues-Scholze-theoretic version of the BM-O bijection at generic parameters.
item.dc:creator: Nikolas Castro

item.title: Positivity of the Mirabolic Quantum Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.39010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we construct the canonical basis for the modified mirabolic quantum $\mathfrak{sl}_n$. We then study the associated $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-module and $\dot{U}_v(\mathfrak{sl}_n)$-comodule structures and prove the positivity of this basis with respect to these two structures.
item.dc:creator: Zhaobing Fan, Haitao Ma, Zhicheng Zhang

item.title: Comparing metric completions of triangulated categories with Verdier quotients
item.description: arXiv:2610.39035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neeman's metric on a triangulated category assigns lengths to morphisms and allows us to construct triangulated metric completions of the category. We prove that the metric completion of a triangulated category with respect to a constant metric is always a subcategory of the Verdier quotient by the thick subcategory generated by cones of zero-length morphisms, and we provide a sufficient criterion for equality. To that end, we define continuous functors between completions which induce triangulated functors between completions. Moreover, we give two applications. First, we show that the additive equivalence discovered by Cummings and Gratz between the Paquette-Yildirim completion and a specific metric completion of an Igusa-Todorov discrete cluster category is, in fact, a triangulated equivalence. Second, we fully classify metric completions of bounded derived categories of coherent sheaves over weighted projective lines of domestic or tubular type.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Matou\v{s}ek

item.title: Affinizations and braided module categories
item.description: arXiv:2610.39456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We relate affinizations of braided monoidal categories to braided module categories, allowing a twist by a braided monoidal automorphism. Our main theorem establishes a bijection between twisted braided structures on a right module category and extensions of its action to the corresponding twisted affinization. We also show that the twisted affinization is the free twisted braided module category on one object. We give explicit presentations of twisted affinizations, both as monoidal categories and as module categories, using invertible dots and reflection relations. We also describe the relation to cylinder twists and tensor-pair cylinder twists, including the naturality condition needed to obtain a braided module structure. As applications, we obtain module-category presentations of the affine Kauffman and affine oriented skein categories and an orientation-reversing twisted version of the latter. We realize the disoriented skein category as a quotient of this twisted affinization by a single additional relation.
item.dc:creator: Hadi Salmasian, Alistair Savage, Yaolong Shen

item.title: Finite-dimensional irreducible representations of Yangians
item.description: arXiv:2610.39589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a direct proof of the well-known classification of finite-dimensional representations of the Yangian $Y(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ following an approach by Chary-Pressley for $U_q(\mathfrak{ \hat sl_2})$.
item.dc:creator: Mikhail Gradov, Aleksei Ilin

item.title: Syzygy-Quiver Formulas and Finitistic Dimensions of Special Biserial Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.39672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite dimensional algebra over a field $\mathbf{k}$. We introduce the reachable syzygy quiver of $\Lambda$, a directed multigraph whose vertices are the isomorphism classes of indecomposable nonprojective direct summands of iterated syzygies of simple modules, and whose arrows record nonprojective summands of first syzygies. The projective dimension of a vertex is one plus its directed path height, allowing the global and finitistic dimensions of $\Lambda$ to be read off from this height function. This formula holds for every finite dimensional algebra, but its states are arbitrary modules. We show that when the first syzygy of an indecomposable module admits a closed combinatorial description from the bound quiver, this state space reduces to a smaller combinatorial quiver, making the global and finitistic dimensions exact computable invariants. We carry this out in three stages. Over a special biserial algebra, the Liu--Morin closure theorem identifies the reachable syzygy quiver with a string-syzygy quiver whose vertices are string modules. Over a string algebra, this compresses to the relation-chain quiver of Xin and Zhang, recovering their global dimension formula along with a parallel formula for the finitistic dimension. Over an arbitrary biserial algebra, the universal formula holds, but uniform compression to paths or strings is impossible, with the Skowro\'nski--Waschb\"usch algebra providing a witness. Finally, we show two string algebras may share the same Gabriel quiver but have distinct global dimensions, proving the ideal of relations is indispensable for these invariants, and we prove that a pointwise homological reduction to a string algebra on the same quiver preserving the monomials of the relations is impossible.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Sardar

item.title: Standardly stratified structures from tilting modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.39805v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Characteristic tilting modules play a central role in the theory of standardly stratified algebras, for instance in Ringel duality. They are constructed from the standard modules, which are determined by a partial order on the simple modules. In this paper, we characterize characteristic tilting modules intrinsically. We show that a tilting module is a characteristic tilting module if and only if the matrix of composition multiplicities of its indecomposable direct summands is triangular with respect to suitable orderings of the summands and of the simple modules. In this case, the standard modules and all the corresponding partial orders are recovered from the tilting module. As an application, we prove that the tilting correspondence of Geiss, Leclerc and Schr\"oer between a GLS path algebra and its associated hereditary algebra restricts to a bijection between characteristic tilting modules. In particular, we obtain GLS path algebras that are not quasi-hereditary with respect to any partial order but for which every tilting module is a characteristic tilting module.
item.dc:creator: Mayu Tsukamoto

item.title: Parahoric Spherical Whittaker Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a non-archimedean local field and let $K_\mu$ be a standard parahoric subgroup of $GL_n(F)$. We express the diagonal values of normalized parahoric Whittaker eigenfunctions with trivial central character using blockwise Casselman--Shalika formulas with the appropriate modulus factor. Every irreducible generic Iwahori-spherical representation has a one-dimensional fixed space for a suitable parahoric, with no invariants under a strictly larger parahoric. The full Hecke character of this line determines the representation. We compute its adjacent-block Hecke eigenvalues and, under additional irreducibility hypotheses, obtain an explicit finite formula on every Bruhat cell using an opposite induced model, Whittaker-preserving intertwiners, and Demazure--Whittaker operators. We apply these formulas to local Rankin--Selberg integrals for $GL_n\times GL_1$ and for compatible parahorics in $GL_n\times GL_m$. In the latter case, the lowest Laurent coefficient and the equal-rank functional equation determine the integral. Explicit translations and rescalings then give test vectors for the local $L$-factor.
item.dc:creator: Markos Karameris

item.title: Harmonic Analysis on $p$-adic Unipotent Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40099v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a $p$-adic unipotent group and let $H$ be an algebraic subgroup of $G$. Given a unitary character $\chi$ of $H$, we consider the monomial representation $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$. To the character $\chi$, we associate the affine subspace $$ X_\chi=f+\mathfrak h^\perp\subset\mathfrak g^*$$ where $f$ is a linear form associated with $\chi$. We describe the irreducible representations occurring in the central decomposition of $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$ in terms of the coadjoint orbits in $\mathfrak g^*$ that meet $X_\chi$. We also determine the corresponding measure class on the unitary dual $\widehat G$. Furthermore, we study the multiplicities of the irreducible representations in this decomposition. As an application, we compute the Plancherel formula for $\operatorname{Ind}_{H}^{G}\chi$ when $H$ is a normal algebraic subgroup of $G$ and the multiplicities are finite.
item.dc:creator: Khemais Maktouf

item.title: Induced representations from the Heisenberg parabolic subgroup of $SL(n+2,\mathbb{R})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The group $G = SL(n+2,\R)$ has a parabolic subgroup $P = MAN$ whose unipotent radical is a Heisenberg group. We study representations induced from a character of $P$, and using the Lie algebra action on the space of $K$-finite vectors we find the points of reducibility and the complementary series. We identify solutions to the conformally invariant systems of differential operators as subrepresentations.
item.dc:creator: Robin van Haastrecht

item.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, reduced and immersed
item.description: arXiv:2610.40602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a `reduced' form of permutation twisted cohomology as introduced by Balmer--Gallauer and further developed by Miller. This ring is bigraded by a well-chosen choice of endotrivial complex, rather than multigraded by a family of endotrivial complexes. The Balmer spectrum of the small derived category of permutation modules openly immerses into the homogeneous spectrum of this ring. We also show that for $p$-groups, Miller's `remixed' twisted cohomology ring also admits the Balmer spectrum as an open subspace, and confirm in both cases it can be upgraded to have Dirac scheme structure; furthermore, we prove that the two open covers witnessing this are in general different.
item.dc:creator: Juan Omar G\'omez, Sam K. Miller

item.title: Partial Airy ideals and coloured blobbed topological recursion
item.description: arXiv:2610.33232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We define and study the notion of partial Airy ideals, which are certain linear systems of PDEs that may contain less equations than variables. We show that they admit a unique solution of exponential type (the partition function) modulo a choice of initial condition. We construct a large class of examples of partial Airy ideals attached to spectral curves using twisted free-field representations of $\mathcal{W}(\mathfrak{gl}_r)$-algebras at self-dual level. This generalizes the results of Bouchard- Borot-Chidambaram-Creutzig-Noshchenko by significantly enlarging the set of admissible spectral curves, provided they come with additional data that we call colour. We show that the differential constraints on the partition function are equivalent to a set of equations on the associated correlators, which we call coloured loop equations. We find a recursive residue formulation for the solutions of those equations, the coloured blobbed topological recursion}, which is a generalization of the currently known forms of topological recursion. It includes the blobbed topological recursion of Borot-Shadrin as a special case, giving it a natural interpretation within the formalism of partial Airy ideals.
item.dc:creator: Ga\"etan Borot, Vincent Bouchard, Swagata S. Datta

item.title: Nijenhuis Lie $n$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.37698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a homotopical framework for Nijenhuis operators on semistrict Lie $n$-algebras ($n$-term $L_\infty$-algebras) for every $n \ge 1$ and, more generally, on arbitrary $L_\infty$-algebras. A Nijenhuis operator is defined as a family $N = (N_q)_{q \ge 1}$ of multilinear maps, with $N_1$ linear, realizing an $L_\infty$-morphism from an $N$-twisted copy of the structure to the original one. We prove that this condition is equivalent to the vanishing, at every arity $m$, of the $m$-th Nijenhuis torsion up to a correction term $\Lambda^N_m$ formed by higher-component substitutions, and we provide a closed combinatorial formula for $\Lambda^N_m$ as a sum over set partitions. Along the way, we show that the arity-$k$ Nijenhuis torsion factors canonically as a composite of $k$ commuting elementary slot deformations. The resulting objects form a category $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$; we establish that $\mathbf{NijLie}_m$ embeds as the full subcategory of $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$ on objects concentrated in the bottom $m$ degrees for all $m \le n$. These levels assemble into a tower whose first three stages are classical Nijenhuis Lie algebras, the Nijenhuis Lie $2$-algebras of Das, and the newly introduced Nijenhuis Lie $3$-algebras. We characterize the strict and skeletal objects at every level, introduce $n$-term representations up to homotopy of a Nijenhuis Lie algebra, and prove that the semidirect product construction establishes an equivalence between the category of such representations and split abelian $\mathbf{NijLie}_n$-extensions. Finally, two corrections to published level-three identities are documented, and all component identities up to arity five are verified via computer algebra.
item.dc:creator: Imed Basdouri, Tarek Ben Massoud, Ahmed Zahari

item.title: Projected Brion's theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.38674v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an analogue of Brion's theorem for the projected integer-point transform. Brion's theorem writes the integer-point transform of a rational polyhedron $P$ as the sum of the rational functions associated to its vertex cones. The pushforward $\pi_*$ along a lattice projection $\pi$ turns the transform of $P$ into the generating function of the numbers of lattice points in the fibres of $\pi$. We group the vertices of $P$ into contracted classes, generated by the edges whose direction $\pi$ kills, and show that the sum of the rational functions associated to the vertex cones in a contracted class can be pushed forward along $\pi$, yielding a rational function decomposition of the projected integer-point transform. For a lattice polytope, the classes correspond to the connected components of the fixed locus of the associated toric variety under the action of a subtorus, and our formula resembles the localization formula for this subtorus. We use this decomposition to provide an explicit formula for the projected integer-point transform of a linear family of polytopes. We illustrate this result with families of Gelfand--Zetlin and string polytopes.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Dupraz, Leonid Monin

item.title: Analysis of blowup masses in constant-coefficient Toda systems: W-invariants and Weyl orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.38905v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify the local blowup masses of constant-coefficient Toda systems for all simple Lie algebras with one prescribed singular source, bounded component masses, and bounded boundary oscillations. We encode the source strengths and the blowup masses by two elements of the Cartan subalgebra: the grading element $p_\mu$ and the mass element $q_\sigma$. We show that $p_\mu-q_\sigma=wp_\mu$ for some Weyl group element $w\in W$. The proof uses the Drinfeld-Sokolov gauge and the resulting holomorphic $W$-invariants for Toda systems. Asymptotic analysis near the source and on a shrinking circle enclosing the total local mass gives two evaluations of the leading Laurent coefficients of the $W$-invariants, which agree by holomorphicity. This agreement enables us to conclude the above Weyl-orbit result. In particular, the quadratic constraint is the local Pohozaev identity. Only with the full set of $W$-invariants can we strengthen earlier orbit-plus-integer restrictions to an exact Weyl-orbit characterization in the constant-coefficient setting. Together with the author's explicit families in [Nie], this determines all attainable local mass vectors.
item.dc:creator: Zhaohu Nie

item.title: PBW theorem for affine super Yangian
item.description: arXiv:2610.38952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a Poincar\'e--Birkhoff--Witt theorem for the distinguished affine super Yangian $Y=Y_{1/2,1/2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}(m|n))$, where $m,n\geq2$ and $m\neq n$. With respect to the current filtration, there is a canonical isomorphism \[ \operatorname{gr}_F Y\cong U\!\left(\operatorname{uce}\!\left( \mathfrak{sl}(m|n)\otimes\mathbb C[z^{\pm1},u] \right)\right), \] where $\operatorname{uce}$ denotes the universal central extension. For any totally ordered classical basis homogeneous in parity and current degree, ordered supermonomials in arbitrary fixed filtered lifts form a vector-space basis of $Y$, with odd exponents restricted to zero or one. The proof identifies the classical presentation through Steinberg Lie superalgebras and establishes injectivity using evaluation homomorphisms, iterated coproducts in degreewise completions, and coefficientwise tensor separation.
item.dc:creator: Vasiliy Volkov, Vladimir Stukopin

item.title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive
item.description: arXiv:2610.39021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.
item.dc:creator: Keith McNulty

item.title: Bases for the Top-Degree Garsia-Haiman Module
item.description: arXiv:2610.39061v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce two new monomial bases for the top $t$-degree component of the Garsia-Haiman module $V_\mu$ for every partition $\mu$. Both bases are indexed by column-strict standard fillings of shape $\mu$; the first has exponents governed by entrywise refinements of Haglund's combinatorial statistics for the modified Macdonald polynomials $\widetilde{H}_\mu(X;q,t)$. The second basis has exponents governed by an insertion algorithm of Bhattacharya-Ratheesh-Viswanath, and gives a basis realization of the ``fermionic formula" of the $m_{1^n}$-coefficient of the $q$-Whittaker polynomial. Our proof uses orbit harmonics, and is inspired by the original approach of Garsia and Haiman.
item.dc:creator: Raymond Chou

item.title: Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics on nilpotent Lie groups and the quasicentroid condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.39184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study left-invariant Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics (cyclic-parallel Ricci tensor) on nilpotent Lie groups, focusing on the algebraic condition that the Ricci operator belongs to the quasicentroid $\operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}$. We review and develop the abstract structure theory of quasicentroids, and prove a Central Decomposition Theorem: any nilpotent Riemannian Lie algebra with $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ decomposes as a central product of ideals $\mathfrak{i}_j = E_{\lambda_j} \oplus \mathfrak{z}$, where $\mathfrak{z}$ is the center of $\mathfrak{n}$ and $E_{\lambda_j}$ are the negative Ricci eigenspaces. Endowed with the restricted metric, each factor $\mathfrak{i}_j$ is itself a Gray $\mathcal{A}$-space. Finally, we investigate when the general $\mathcal{A}$-metric condition reduces to $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$. We prove this equivalence unconditionally for two-step nilpotent algebras and whenever the metric admits a nice basis, and provide a general characterization via the vanishing of two trace identities.
item.dc:creator: Edison Alberto Fern\'{a}ndez-Culma

item.title: Quasimodularity of $q$-series associated to root lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.40034v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by conjectures arising in part from the study of class-$\mathcal{S}$ vertex algebras associated with four-dimensional supersymmetric field theories, we study multiple $q$-zeta functions attached to finite-dimensional simple Lie algebras. We prove their conjectured quasimodularity for all classical Lie algebras of types $A$, $B$, $C$, and $D$, as well as a more general Weyl-symmetrized version in which the exponents attached to the positive roots are allowed to vary, under a suitable parity condition. Our proof is based on a substantially more general result. We introduce new combinatorial objects, called sets of level one and pairs of level two, which generalize the configurations arising from classical root systems. To these we associate multivariable lattice sums and prove that, under a natural admissibility condition, they are Fourier expansions of polar quasi-Jacobi forms of level one and level two, respectively. Quasimodularity of the Lie-theoretic $q$-series follows by specialization of the elliptic variables. The positive roots of type $A$ form a set of level one, and those of types $B$, $C$, and $D$ are described by pairs of level two. The proof combines a structural analysis of these new combinatorial configurations with reduction procedures and induction on the rank. The resulting framework applies to a much wider class of lattice sums than those coming from root systems and supports more general quasimodularity conjectures for $q$-series associated with integral hyperplane arrangements.
item.dc:creator: Antun Milas, Jan-Willem M. van Ittersum

item.title: Quantum cluster structures on bosonic extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.40058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a quantum cluster algebra structure on the standard $\mathbb Z[q^{\pm1/2}]$-form of the bosonic extension algebra $\widehat A(b)$ for every positive braid $b$ and every symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix. The proof realizes this algebra as the degree-zero part of a localization of a larger quantum unipotent coordinate ring, obtained by thickening a word for $b$. For symmetric Cartan matrices, this realization also gives a monoidal categorification of the quantum cluster algebra.
item.dc:creator: Yingjin Bi

item.title: On stable twist 2-groups of quasi-Hopf algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.40228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any finite-dimensional quasi-Hopf algebra $A$, we define the notion of a stable twist of $A$. We show that stable twists form a strict 2-group $\2ust(A)$, which is equivalent to $\OAut(\C{A})^{\rev}$. Given a group homomorphism $\rho: G \to \ost(A)$, we determine the obstruction in $H^3(G,Z_G(A))$ to lift $\rho$ to a $G$-action on $\C{A}$. We also establish a bijection between such liftings and cocentral cleft extensions of $\k[G]$ by $A$. The main application of $\2ust(A)$ is the computation of $\OAut(\C{A})$, together with an explicit description of the corresponding tensor autoequivalences. We apply this framework to pointed Hopf algebras $A$ that arise as central extensions of Taft algebras by cyclic groups, and we explicitly determine all of their tensor autoequivalences. The equivariantizations of $\C{A}$ by $\ost(A)$ produce a new family of Hopf algebras $\N(n,\xi)$ of dimension $2nm$, where $\xi$ is a scalar of order $m\mid n$ such that neither $\N(n,\xi)$ nor its dual has the Chevalley property. In dimension 24, we prove that $\N(6,-1)$ and its dual are precisely the Hopf algebras $H$ for which neither $H$ nor $H^*$ has the Chevalley property. This completes the classification of nonsemisimple Hopf algebras of dimension 24.
item.dc:creator: Siu-Hung Ng, Xingting Wang

item.title: An Arithmetic Property of Intertwining Operators for Real Reductive Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be the group of complex points of a connected split reductive group defined over ${\mathbb Q}$. We study the standard intertwining operator between representations parabolically induced from essentially tempered cohomological representations of Levi subgroups of maximal parabolic subgroups. Under certain algebraicity, purity, and criticality hypotheses, the operator is holomorphic and invertible at a particular point of evaluation. The relative Lie algebra cohomology of these induced representations is one-dimensional in the lowest nonzero degree. Under prescribed rational generators of these one-dimensional spaces, we show that the intertwining operator is a nonzero rational multiple of a certain product of ratios of local $L$-factors. This is a cohomological version of Langlands's calculation of the Gindikin-Karplevic formula. The main theorem provides a local input for the arithmetic study of special values of Langlands--Shahidi $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: A. Raghuram, Xin Zou

item.title: Galois module structure of Deligne--Lusztig varieties for $\mathrm{GL}_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.40335v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)\to\overline{\mathbf{X}}(w)$ be the ramified Galois cover of compactified Deligne--Lusztig varieties. Our objects of study are the Lefschetz numbers for the action of the finite covering group $T^{wF}$ on the coherent cohomology of the structure sheaf of $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$. The Lefschetz numbers for all elements of $T^{wF}$ determine the virtual $T^{wF}$-representation given by the alternating sum of these cohomology groups. In the two cases of Deligne--Lusztig surfaces of type $A_2$ and ${}^{2}A_2$, we give explicit formulas for the Lefschetz numbers for a generator of the stabilizer of an irreducible component. It follows that the equivariant Euler characteristic of the compactification $\overline{\mathbf{Y}}(w)$ is not virtually free as a virtual module over the covering group.
item.dc:creator: Adithya Sathyanarayana

item.title: Frobenius kernels of algebraic supergroups and Steinberg's tensor product theorem
item.description: arXiv:2206.06000v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a split quasireductive supergroup $G$ defined over a field, we study structure and representation of Frobenius kernels $G_r$ of $G$ and we give a necessary and sufficient condition for $G_r$ to be unimodular in terms of the root system of $G$. We also establish Steinberg's tensor product theorem for $G$ under some natural assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Taiki Shibata

item.title: Archimedean period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions
item.description: arXiv:2412.18805v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate and prove the archimedean period relations for Rankin-Selberg convolutions of $\text{GL}(n)\times \text{GL}(n)$ and $\text{GL}(n)\times \text{GL}(n-1)$, for all generic cohomological representations. As a consequence, we prove the non-vanishing of the archimedean modular symbols. This extends the earlier results in [LLS24] for essentially tempered representations of $\text{GL}(n)\times\text{GL}(n-1)$.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Jin, Dongwen Liu, Binyong Sun

item.title: On the source algebra equivalence class of blocks with cyclic defect groups, II
item.description: arXiv:2502.09176v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This series of papers is a contribution to the program of classifying $p$-blocks of finite groups up to source algebra equivalence, starting with the case of cyclic blocks. To any $p$-block $\mathbf{B}$ of a finite group with cyclic defect group $D$, Linckelmann associated an invariant $W( \mathbf{B} )$, which is an indecomposable endo-permutation module over $D$, and which, together with the Brauer tree of $\mathbf{B}$, essentially determines its source algebra equivalence class. In Parts II-IV of our series of papers, we classify, for odd $p$, those endo-permutation modules of cyclic $p$-groups arising from $p$-blocks of quasisimple groups. In the present Part II, we reduce the desired classification for the quasisimple classical groups of Lie type $B$, $C$, and $D$ to the corresponding objective for the general linear and unitary groups; the classification is completed for the latter groups.
item.dc:creator: Gerhard Hiss, Caroline Lassueur

item.title: Rational structures on quivers and a generalization of Gelfand's equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2506.23251v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notion of rational structure on a quiver and associated representations to establish a coherent framework for studying quiver representations in separable field extensions. This notion is linked to a refinement of the notion of $K$-species, which we term \'etale $K$-species. We establish a categorical anti-equivalence between $K$-rational quivers and \'etale $K$-species, which extends to an equivalence of their respective representation categories. For $K$-rational quivers there is a canonical notion of base change, which suggests a corresponding notion of base change for (\'etale) $K$-species which we elaborate. As a primary application, we generalize Gelfand's celebrated equivalence between certain blocks of Harish-Chandra modules for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and representations of the Gelfand quiver to a rational setting. To this end, we define a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational structure on the Gelfand quiver and its representations. A key technical tool, which we call unipotent stabilization, is developed to construct the functor from rational Harish-Chandra modules to nilpotent rational quiver representations. We prove that this functor is an equivalence. A similar result is established for the cyclic quiver. Both results hold over every field $E$ of characteristic $0$, for suitable $E$-rational structures on the two quivers; for $E=\mathbb{C}$ they recover Gelfand's equivalence. In this rational framework the defining relation of the Gelfand quiver acquires a descent-theoretic meaning: its Galois orbit is stable, it descends to a single relation on the associated $\mathbb{Q}$-species, and a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational representation satisfies it if and only if the composite of the two arrows through the vertex $-$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-rational endomorphism of the space at the central vertex. This allows us to recast our results in the language of $\mathbb{Q}$-species.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Januszewski

item.title: Quivers with involutions and shifted twisted Yangians via Coulomb branches
item.description: arXiv:2510.12118v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To a quiver with involution, we study the Coulomb branch of the 3d $\mathcal{N} = 4$ involution-fixed part of the quiver gauge theory. We show that there is an algebra homomorphism from the corresponding shifted twisted Yangian to the quantized Coulomb branch algebra. This gives a new instance of 3D mirror symmetries.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Communications in Mathematical Physics 407 (2026), Paper No. 244
item.dc:creator: Yaolong Shen, Changjian Su, Rui Xiong

item.title: Perverse filtration on the cohomology of affine Springer fibers
item.description: arXiv:2606.01507v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the top cohomology of any affine Springer fiber, as a Weyl group representation, contains a large part of the total cohomology of certain Springer fibers. The main ingredient of the proof is the construction of a ``perverse filtration'' on the pure part of the cohomology of affine Springer fibers.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwei Yun

item.title: Archimedean Modular Symbols for Rankin-Selberg Convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$
item.description: arXiv:2607.19133v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We explicit calculate the archimedean modular symbol for Rankin-Selberg convolutions of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{C})\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$, for all generic cohomological representations.
item.dc:creator: Yubo Jin, Zeyu Tian

item.title: Categorification in Representation Theory
item.description: arXiv:2608.19830v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this survey article, we give an introduction to the relatively young subject of $2$-representation theory, which studies categorifications of important players in classical representation theory. In particular, we provide a streamlined exposition of the main results leading to the classification of simple $2$-representations for Soergel bimodules associated to finite Weyl groups in characteristic $0$, obtained in [M. Mackaay, V. Mazorchuk, V. Miemietz, D. Tubbenhauer and X. Zhang, Simple transitive $2$-representations of Soergel bimodules for finite Coxeter types. Proc. London Math. Soc. 126 (2023)].
item.dc:creator: Vanessa Miemietz

item.title: Total positivity in coordinate algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.01321v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define the totally positive part of the coordinate algebra associated to a Cartan datum of simply laced type. We show its relation to the canonical basis of the corresponding plus part of the enveloping algebra.
item.dc:creator: G. Lusztig

item.title: Webs and finite dimensional representation theory for quantum symmetric pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.08057v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a highest weight framework and construct explicit finite dimensional irreducible modules for the type AIII (quasi split) quantum symmetric pair subalgebras $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$. In Part 1, we provide a uniform construction of Cartan subalgebras and Verma modules for both subfamilies. Our construction recovers Letzter's Cartan subalgebra in one subfamily and gives a new Cartan subalgebra in the other. We construct a weak triangular decomposition of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$ via the Letzter map. Then we define Verma modules as induced modules and prove that finite dimensional simple $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$-modules are quotients of our Verma modules. In Part 2, we define a diagrammatic category $Web^B$ that controls polynomial representations of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$. We prove a multiplicity-free decomposition of the quantum exterior powers $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$ as a $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$-module, using a explicit eigenspace decomposition of certain dot morphisms in $Web^B$. As applications, we deduce the multiplicity-freeness of the involved anti-spherical Hecke module. For $\bigwedge^k\mathbb{V}$, we explicitly determine the highest weight vectors and their weights, thereby determining the isomorphism classes of their irreducible summands. Finally, we determine the kernel of the $Web^B$-action on certain finite dimensional representation category of $U_q'(\mathfrak{gl}_n^\theta)$.
item.dc:creator: Liao Wang

item.title: Extending Upper Cluster Algebras
item.description: arXiv:1707.04661v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $S$ be an upper cluster algebra, which is a subalgebra of $R$. Suppose that there is some cluster variable $x_e$ such that ${R}_{{x}_e} = S[{x}_e^{\pm 1}]$. We try to understand under which conditions ${R}$ is an upper cluster algebra, and how the quiver of $R$ relates to that of $S$. Moreover, if the restriction of $(\Delta,W)$ to some subquiver is a cluster model, we give a sufficient condition for $(\Delta,W)$ itself being a cluster model. As an application, we show that the semi-invariant ring of any complete $m$-tuple flags is an upper cluster algebra whose quiver is explicitly given. Moreover, the quiver with its rigid potential is a polyhedral cluster model.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei, Jerzy Weyman

item.title: The $q$-deformed random-to-random family in the Hecke algebra
item.description: arXiv:2503.17580v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We generalize Reiner--Saliola--Welker's well-known but mysterious family of *$k$-random-to-random shuffles* from Markov chains on symmetric groups to Markov chains on Type-$A$ Iwahori--Hecke algebras. We prove that these operators pairwise commute, and that their eigenvalues are polynomials in $q$ with non-negative integer coefficients; we express these eigenvalues in a closed form as certain symmetric function evaluations (which is new even for $q=1$). We show that these operators are simultaneously diagonalizable for almost all $q$, and combinatorially express the dimension of the subalgebra they generate. Our work generalizes and extends work of Reiner--Saliola--Welker and Lafreni\`ere for the symmetric group, and simplifies all known proofs in this case.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Brauner, Patricia Commins, Darij Grinberg, Franco Saliola

item.title: On the Blasius-Deligne conjecture for the standard $L$-functions of symplectic type
item.description: arXiv:2509.00434v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Blasius-Deligne conjecture for automorphic $L$-functions is about the period relations and the algebraicity of critical $L$-values. In this paper, we prove the Blasius-Deligne conjecture for standard $L$-functions attached to regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representations of $GL_{2n}$ of symplectic type, under the expected Galois invariance condition for these representations. The main results extend the classical work of G. Shimura and Y. Manin from $GL_2$ to $GL_{2n}$, and complete the approach that was initially taken by H. Grobner and A. Raghuram and by F. Januszewski, where a few technical assumptions were taken.
item.dc:creator: Dihua Jiang, Dongwen Liu, Binyong Sun, Fangyang Tian

item.title: The symmetric hit problem in four variables: Relative cohits and stabilizer-fixed preimages
item.description: arXiv:2606.02626v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we study the symmetric hit problem in four variables by analyzing the relative cohit space, defined as the kernel of the inclusion-induced map from symmetric to ordinary cohits. We establish that this relative space is isomorphic to a kernel in the first group cohomology of the permutation group and, equivalently, to an $\operatorname{Ext}^1$ kernel for the general linear group, equipped with a canonical action of the normalizer quotient. We use explicit Lucas--Cartan identities to construct unconditional fixed Steenrod preimages for nontrivial stabilizers, resolving infinite families of monomials strictly above the minimal-spike weight. Using the ordinary and symmetric Kameko isomorphisms, we reduce the determination of complete bases in two generic degree families to exact calculations in degrees one, three, six, ten, and sixteen. The relative space first becomes nonzero in degree fifteen, where it is one-dimensional, and it is an indecomposable two-dimensional normalizer module in degree eighteen. In the family $5\cdot2^t-4$, the symmetric cohit dimension stabilizes at six and the relative dimension at one for $t\geq2$; in the family $7\cdot2^t-4$, they are four and zero for $t\geq1$. We give complete bases by explicit exponent formulas and prove Janfada's monomial implication [7, Conjecture 1] in every degree of both families. We extend the known optimal bound for ordinary Kameko isomorphisms to every permutation-invariant cohit space, prove its optimality there, and transport the entire symmetric hit basis by a direct-sum formula.
item.dc:creator: Dang Vo Phuc, Peter V. Danchev

item.title: A new proof of characteristic-free Kn\"orrer periodicity
item.description: arXiv:2609.37839v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $R = S/(f)$ be a complete local hypersurface ring and let $A = S[\![u,v]\!]/(f+uv)$. Pfister and Popescu showed that the stable categories of maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules over $R$ and over $A$ are equivalent, with no assumption on the characteristic. We give a short proof. If $(\Phi,\Psi)$ is a matrix factorization of $h$ and $\partial$ is a derivation, then $(\partial\Psi,\partial\Phi)$ is a null-homotopy for multiplication by $\partial h$. Since $u$ and $v$ are partial derivatives of $f+uv$, they act as zero on the stable category of $A$, so the Koszul complex on $u$ and $v$ splits in the singularity category, and this gives density. For the double branched cover $S[\![z]\!]/(f+z^2)$ the same argument yields $2z$: it recovers Kn\"orrer's lemma up to free summands on the double branched cover when $2$ is a unit, and we show by an example that this lemma, and periodicity for the iterated double branched cover $S[\![z,w]\!]/(f+z^2+w^2)$, fail in characteristic two. We also compute the second syzygy over $A$ of a maximal Cohen-Macaulay $R$-module by an explicit resolution, and show that the change of basis used there cannot be given by a universal matrix formula.
item.dc:creator: Graham J. Leuschke

item.title: Zero-free half-planes for Hecke $L$-functions over number fields and Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis
item.description: arXiv:2610.26835v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In [Liu26a], varying the length and moment parameters in the cubic-theta argument of [Ope26a] gave the zero-free half-plane $Re(s)>B_{\mathrm{new}}=0.874957019420098946\ldots$ for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and for Dirichlet $L$-functions, and its optimality in the specified exponent comparison system. In this paper, we extend the argument to finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over cyclotomic fields containing $\mu_{12}$ and, by class-field descent, to every pair $(K,\eta)$ whose cyclic class field has metabelian normal closure over $\mathbb Q$, including every finite-order character over every abelian number field. Then, adapting the averaged numerator estimate developed by Xu and Sang [XS26] for Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and combining it with a limiting contradiction argument, we obtain the boundary $B_\flat=0.874886647039964\ldots$, the root near $0.8749$ of $133488B^4-376596B^3+384534B^2-167541B+26231$; it is the exact infimum of the refined comparison system, unattained by finite chains starting above it. Since the analytic argument uses only $\mu_{12}\subset F$, we run it over $F=K(\zeta_{12})$ for an arbitrary number field $K$ and descend: every finite-order Hecke $L$-function over every number field is zero-free for $Re(s)>B_\flat$, giving a uniform Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis over number fields. The analytic argument uses the exceptional-theta constructions and local calculations of the preprint [Ope26b].
item.dc:creator: Baiying Liu
